normalization.overview: Matt Pocock demonstrates an engineering workflow with domain vocabulary, adversarial questioning, specifications, architectural seams, worktrees, types, tests and review. This Reader examines how inexpensive generation changes the cost of accepting and maintaining software work.
normalization.whyItMatters: When generating candidates becomes cheap, intent, independent verification, integration, release and later maintenance can become the limiting stages. Better tools and design may reduce these costs; the effect depends on the task and must be tested.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Measure accepted, maintainable outcomes per unit of total effort. Preserve durable intent and bounded seams, test the actual property and keep verification, authorization and deployment distinct. Scale review and coordination to the real risk.
normalization.falsification: Compare representative tasks under a fixed acceptance standard across baseline assistance, a versioned specification and seam, and increased concurrency. Count accepted outcomes, total effort, review backlog, admitted unresolved properties, escaped defects and later rework; keep interventions only if benefits exceed costs without unacceptable degradation.
normalization.freshness: Interview November 20, 2026; primary research and public documentation checked November 24, 2026 PT. Eight segment candidates staged under structural schemas, not semantic validation. Twenty-eight cue/chapter anchors checked. The interview's method is not independently performance-tested; illustrative economics are not observations.

claims.proposition: The early-2025 METR randomized study observed 19% longer task time with AI tools in its study setting.
claims.assessment: 16 experienced open-source developers, 246 tasks; 95% CI +2% to +39%. This is evidence of the specified setting, not a universal effect.
claims.limits: Studied early-2025 tools and mature codebases. Later tools, participants, selection and measurement may differ.

claims.proposition: The February 2026 METR update reports uncertain later task-time estimates.
claims.assessment: Original-participant subset estimate minus 18% with CI minus 38% to plus 9%; new recruits minus 4% with CI minus 15% to plus 9%. The update describes later evidence as weak or unreliable.
claims.limits: Selection and concurrent-agent timing issues undermine confident generalization; intervals span no difference.

claims.proposition: The earlier Copilot controlled experiment reported 55.8% faster completion of a bounded HTTP-server task.

claims.limits: One bounded JavaScript implementation task; no long-term maintenance, integration or deployment measurement.

relationships.reason: Examines how cheap code generation shifts the meaningful standard from raw output to ambitious accepted value. This Reader adds a conditional economics of the engineering effort required to accept and maintain the next change.

Distinguishes reusable context from durable governed knowledge and accepted work. This Reader extends that argument to domain vocabulary, architectural decisions and module seams that reduce the obligation to rediscover intent.

sharePlaneRelationships.title: The Confidence to Delegate
sharePlaneRelationships.reason: Examines the distinction between capability and authority, and why operational assurance and recovery determine warranted delegation. It complements the trust ladder and the boundary between verified behavior and release permission.
